duplicates.fix: In IndexService.DropIndex, after deleting each node call _snapshot.AddOrRemoveFreeIndexList(node.Page, ref index.FreeIndexPageList) (which deletes the page when ItemsCount reaches 0), and do the same for the head/tail page, so emptied pages join _transPages' deleted-page list and reach _header.FreeEmptyPageList on commit.
duplicates.rationale: Same leak as [40], reported from the Engine/Index.cs entry point.

duplicates.title: AesStream derives its blank-page sentinel from an ArrayPool buffer that is never zeroed, so encrypted blank-page detection can silently break
duplicates.mech: `msBuffer = _bufferPool.Rent(16)` comes from the process-wide ArrayPool<byte>.Shared, which makes no guarantee that rented content is zeroed (only the Return(..., true) at line 166 clears it, and any other component in the process may return a dirty 16-byte array without clearing). The constructor then decrypts whatever is in msBuffer into _decryptedZeroes (lines 151-155), even though the field is meant to hold AES-decrypt(16 zero bytes) - it is the sentinel used by IsBlank() in Read() to recognise pages whose ciphertext is all zeros and blank them out.
duplicates.fail: Any library in the same process rents and returns a <=16 byte array from ArrayPool<byte>.Shared without clearing it (the 16-byte bucket is the smallest shared bucket). The next encrypted LiteDB open computes _decryptedZeroes = decrypt(garbage). A log page whose ciphertext is all zeros (file extended by SetLength, or a torn write) now decrypts to a fixed non-zero plaintext, so AesStream.Read no longer blanks it and PageBuffer.IsBlank() returns false. WalIndexService.RestoreIndex then treats the garbage plaintext as a real page header: it reads a bogus pageID/transactionID and, if the byte at P_IS_CONFIRMED happens to be non-zero, calls ConfirmTransaction for it, publishing a garbage page into the WAL index (and if the bogus page type reads as Header, overwriting the in-memory header page) instead of skipping the page as designed.
duplicates.fix: Use a local `new byte[16]` (or Array.Clear the rented buffer right after Rent) before decrypting it into _decryptedZeroes. While here, note the sibling assumption at lines 121/143: `checkBuffer.All(x => x == 0/1)` scans the whole rented array, which is only correct because Rent(32) currently returns exactly 32 bytes - use the explicit 32-byte range instead.
duplicates.rationale: Same unzeroed-rent sentinel as [54], reported at the Rent call.

duplicates.title: LiteFileStream.Flush() throws NullReferenceException on a read-mode stream
duplicates.mech: `Flush()` unconditionally calls `WriteChunks(true)`, whose first act is `_buffer.Seek(0, SeekOrigin.Begin)` (LiteFileStream.Write.cs:36). `_buffer` is only assigned in the `FileAccess.Write` branch of the constructor (LiteFileStream.cs:42), so it is null for every stream returned by `OpenRead()`/`LiteFileInfo.OpenRead()`. `Stream.Flush()` is contractually required to be a harmless no-op on non-writable streams (that is why `Stream` itself implements it as empty), and callers routinely call it defensively. `Write()` has the same defect: it never checks `_mode` and dereferences the null `_buffer` instead of throwing `NotSupportedException` as `CanWrite == false` promises.
duplicates.fix: `if (_mode != FileAccess.Write) return;` at the top of `Flush()`, and `if (_mode != FileAccess.Write) throw new NotSupportedException();` at the top of `Write()`.
duplicates.rationale: Same null _buffer dereference as [61].

duplicates.title: ABS() throws OverflowException for Int32.MinValue / Int64.MinValue
duplicates.mech: `Math.Abs(int)` and `Math.Abs(long)` are documented to throw OverflowException for `MinValue` because the negation has no representable result. ABS dispatches on the BsonType and calls them directly with no guard, and the expression engine invokes the static method through a compiled `Expression.Call` with no exception wrapping (methods are bound reflectively in LiteDB/Document/Expression/BsonExpression.cs:430).
duplicates.fail: Document `{v: -2147483648}` (Int32.MinValue, a perfectly storable value). `db.Execute("SELECT ABS($.v) FROM col")` throws `System.OverflowException: Negating the minimum value of a twos complement number is invalid` out of the query pipeline. Same for `{v: -9223372036854775808}` via the Int64 branch on line 21.
duplicates.fix: Widen before negating: for Int32 return `Math.Abs((long)value.AsInt32)`; for Int64 special-case `long.MinValue` (return the decimal/double magnitude) instead of calling Math.Abs.
duplicates.rationale: The ABS half of [123].

duplicates.title: ROUND() passes an unvalidated digit count to Math.Round, throwing ArgumentOutOfRangeException
duplicates.mech: `Math.Round(double, int)` requires 0 <= digits <= 15 and `Math.Round(decimal, int)` requires 0 <= digits <= 28; both throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException otherwise. ROUND only checks that `digits.IsNumber`, then forwards `digits.AsInt32`. `AsInt32` is `Convert.ToInt32(RawValue)`, which itself throws OverflowException for a large Double argument. No guard exists in the callers (the method is bound reflectively and invoked directly).
duplicates.fail: `db.Execute("SELECT ROUND(1.567, -1)")` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Rounding digits must be between 0 and 15`. `db.Execute("SELECT ROUND(1.567, 99)")` throws the same. `db.Execute("SELECT ROUND(1.5, 1e20)")` throws OverflowException from `Convert.ToInt32`. All are ordinary query input and all escape as non-LiteDB exceptions.
duplicates.fix: Clamp/validate: reject or clamp `digits` to [0,15] for Double and [0,28] for Decimal, returning BsonValue.Null or a LiteException with a clear message instead of letting BCL argument exceptions escape.
duplicates.rationale: The ROUND half of [123].

duplicates.title: DATEDIFF('s'/'m') overflows Int32 for date ranges beyond ~68 years
duplicates.mech: The second/minute/hour/day branches compute `Convert.ToInt32(Math.Truncate(end.Subtract(start).TotalSeconds))`. `Convert.ToInt32(double)` throws OverflowException once the value exceeds int.MaxValue (2147483647). For the 's' unit that threshold is only ~68.1 years of difference, well inside the DateTime range LiteDB stores.
duplicates.fail: `db.Execute("SELECT DATEDIFF('s', DATETIME('1900-01-01'), DATETIME('2020-01-01'))")`: the interval is ~3.786e9 seconds, so `Convert.ToInt32` throws `OverflowException: Value was either too large or too small for an Int32` instead of returning a value. Same with any stored pair of dates more than 68 years apart, e.g. a birthdate column diffed against now in seconds.
duplicates.fix: Return Int64 for these units (`(long)Math.Truncate(...)`) — BsonValue supports Int64 — or clamp with a LiteException explaining the unit overflowed.
duplicates.rationale: Same DATEDIFF Int32 narrowing as [124].

duplicates.title: A JSON object with an empty key crashes JsonReader with IndexOutOfRangeException
duplicates.mech: ReadObject() accepts any String token as a key (Expect on line 115 permits String/Word) and then indexes it unconditionally: `if (key[0] == '$' && obj.Count == 0)`. Tokenizer.ReadString (LiteDB/Utils/Tokenizer.cs:624) returns String.Empty for the input `""` - its loop simply terminates on the immediate closing quote - so key can legitimately be the empty string. `key[0]` then throws IndexOutOfRangeException. The && short-circuit does not help because key[0] is the left operand. This escapes as a raw runtime exception rather than the LiteException.UnexpectedToken the parser produces for every other malformed input.
duplicates.fail: `LiteDB.JsonSerializer.Deserialize("{\"\": 1}")` - valid JSON with an empty property name, routinely produced by JavaScript clients and by `JSON.stringify` over objects with an empty key - throws System.IndexOutOfRangeException out of ReadObject. A caller that wraps LiteDB parsing in `catch (LiteException)` (the documented failure mode) does not catch it, so the exception propagates past the application's input-validation boundary and, when it happens inside a db.Execute/insert pipeline, leaves the caller unable to distinguish bad input from an engine fault.
duplicates.fix: Test the length first: `if (key.Length > 0 && key[0] == '$' && obj.Count == 0)` (or reject empty keys with LiteException.UnexpectedToken if empty property names are not supported).
duplicates.rationale: Same unchecked key[0] as [126].

duplicates.title: WriteIndexKey's only key-size guard is DEBUG-only, and the length it records is an unchecked (ushort) truncation
duplicates.mech: `DEBUG(...)` is `[Conditional("DEBUG")]` (Constants.cs:184-186), unlike `ENSURE` which throws in every configuration. So in Release builds `WriteIndexKey` performs no size validation at all before writing into the slice, and the length it records is `(ushort)Encoding.UTF8.GetByteCount(str)` (line 328) / `(ushort)arr.Length` (line 340) -- an unchecked narrowing conversion. The only real backstop is `ExtendedLengthHelper.WriteLength`, which throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for length > 1023; but that check runs on the *already truncated* value, so a 65536-byte key wraps to 0 and passes validation while 65536 bytes are actually written. Separately, the one caller that is not pre-validated -- `SortContainer.Insert` (SortContainer.cs:70) -- writes the key *before* computing and range-checking `keyLength` at lines 72-74, so the friendly `LiteException.InvalidIndexKey("Sort key must be less than 1023 bytes.")` can never be the exception the user sees for an oversized key. I traced the overflow itself and could not make it escape the slice (SortService.YieldValues caps a container's accumulated key lengths at CONTAINER_SORT_SIZE and IndexService.AddNode range-checks keyLength before InsertIndexNode), so this is a hardening/error-quality gap rather than a live corruption path.
duplicates.fail: ORDER BY on a non-indexed field whose value is a 5000-byte string: BasePipe.OrderBy -> SortContainer.Insert calls buffer.WriteIndexKey first, so WriteLength throws `System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Specified argument was out of the range of valid values. (Parameter 'length')` out of the user's ToList(), instead of the LiteException.InvalidIndexKey message that the very next two lines were written to produce. With a large document/array or vector sort key instead, WriteLength is bypassed entirely and the user gets LiteException.InvalidDatafileState("current value must fit inside defined buffer") or ArgumentException("Destination array was not long enough") -- three different misleading errors for one condition.
duplicates.fix: Promote the guard to `ENSURE` (or an explicit LiteException.InvalidIndexKey) so it runs in Release, check the untruncated `int` byte count before casting to ushort, and move SortContainer's keyLength check above the WriteIndexKey call.
duplicates.rationale: Same write-before-validate ordering as [72], plus the observations that WriteIndexKey's only size guard is DEBUG-only and the recorded length is an unchecked (ushort) truncation. The author explicitly could not make the overflow escape the slice, so only the error-quality part is established.

duplicates.title: LiteEngine.Checkpoint() throws LockRecursionException when called on a thread that has an open transaction
duplicates.mech: `LockService` uses a single `ReaderWriterLockSlim` created with `LockRecursionPolicy.NoRecursion` (LiteDB/Engine/Services/LockService.cs:20). Every open transaction holds that lock in *read* mode (`EnterTransaction` -> `TryEnterReadLock`). `LockService.EnterExclusive()` only short-circuits on `_transaction.IsWriteLockHeld`; it has no `IsReadLockHeld` guard and goes straight to `TryEnterWriteLock(_pragmas.Timeout)`. `ReaderWriterLockSlim` with `NoRecursion` explicitly refuses a read->write upgrade: `TryEnterWriteLockCore` checks `lrwc.readercount > 0` and throws `LockRecursionException("Write lock may not be acquired with read lock held...")`. So the exclusive-lock acquisition in `Checkpoint()` faults instead of blocking or returning. Note that `TryCheckpoint()` at line 295 *does* have the guard (`TryEnterExclusive` tests `IsReadLockHeld || CurrentReadCount > 0` first) - the hard `Checkpoint()` path is the only one missing it, and checkpoint is the only caller of `EnterExclusive` in the whole engine.
duplicates.fail:
```
using var db = new LiteDatabase("data.db");
db.GetCollection("c").Insert(new BsonDocument { ["a"] = 1 }); // log now has a confirmed tx, well under the 1000-page auto-checkpoint
db.BeginTrans();                                              // this thread now holds the transaction read lock
db.Checkpoint();                                              // <-- throws
```
The early-return guard is passed (log length > 0, `_confirmTransactions.Count == 1`), then `EnterExclusive()` raises `System.Threading.LockRecursionException` - a raw framework exception, not a `LiteException`, with a message about lock recursion that tells the caller nothing about transactions. It escapes `LiteEngine.Checkpoint()` untouched (no `_state.Handle` wrapping on this path), and the open transaction is left dangling.
duplicates.fix: Either give `EnterExclusive()` the same read-lock guard `TryEnterExclusive` has and surface a clear error (`throw new LiteException(0, "Cannot checkpoint inside an open transaction")`), or have `WalIndexService.Checkpoint()` detect `_locker.IsInTransaction` up front and throw that domain exception.
duplicates.rationale: Same missing IsReadLockHeld guard as [5], reported from WalIndexService.Checkpoint.

duplicates.title: Recycled readable frames are published without clearing, so a short/EOF read publishes a previously cached page's bytes as the requested page
duplicates.mech: The readable-miss path in GetReadablePage takes a frame straight off the free list (`_reclaimer.AcquireFrameLocked()`), and `TransitionFreeToLoadingLocked` does NOT zero it -- it only resets Position/Origin/ShareCounter/State. In Release builds the frame's 8192 bytes are exactly whatever the previous occupant (an unrelated cached page) left there; `TransitionToFreeLocked` poisons the bytes only under `#if DEBUG || TESTING` (MemoryCache.cs:356-361). The whole design therefore depends on the `factory` delegate overwriting all PAGE_SIZE bytes. The only production factory, `DiskReader.ReadStream` (LiteDB/Engine/Disk/DiskReader.cs:81), does `stream.Read(buffer.Array, buffer.Offset, buffer.Count)` and DISCARDS the return value -- no loop, no length check. When the read returns fewer than 8192 bytes (0 at/past EOF for FileStream; a partial `CryptoStream` read through AesStream.Read, whose own return value is also dropped), the frame keeps the old page's tail, and MemoryCache.cs:136-142 then publishes that frame as `FrameState.Readable` and inserts it in `_index`/`_sharedReads` as the authoritative content of `position`. Contrast GetWritablePage, which does `writable.Clear()` before calling the factory (MemoryCache.cs:190) -- only the readable path is unprotected. The one guard that was meant to catch this, `DEBUG(buffer.All(0) == false, "check if are not reading out of file length")` at DiskReader.cs:83, is now dead code in this fork precisely because freed frames are filled with 0xFF rather than left zeroed, so `All(0)` can never be true.
duplicates.fail: Open a data file whose tail was lost (crash between `SetLength` and the header flush, or a second process in shared mode shrank it) so `_header.LastPageID`/the free-page chain still names pageID 40 while the file holds only 10 pages. Earlier in the session page 5 was cached and then evicted, leaving frame F holding page 5's 8192 bytes on the free list. `Snapshot.GetPage(40)` -> `DiskReader.ReadPage(327680, writable:false, Data)` -> `GetReadablePage` misses, gets frame F, calls `ReadStream`, which seeks to 327680 and gets `Read(...) == 0` (past EOF) -- return value discarded. MemoryCache publishes F as Readable for key 327680 with page 5's full contents. `BasePage.ReadPage` then parses a structurally valid page: PageID field reads 5, PageType/ItemCount/footer slots all valid, so LiteDB treats page 40 as a live copy of page 5 and follows page 5's NextPageID/index pointers under page 40's identity -- queries return documents from the wrong page as if correct, and if page 40 is subsequently modified and written to the log, page 5's content is persisted on disk under a second pageID. Had the frame been zeroed, the same read would have produced PageID 0 / PageType 0 and raised a clean InvalidPageType / InvalidDatafileState instead of silently wrong data.
duplicates.fix: Either clear the frame in `TransitionFreeToLoadingLocked` (symmetric with `GetWritablePage`'s `writable.Clear()`), or make the loader contract explicit and enforce it: have `DiskReader.ReadStream` loop until PAGE_SIZE bytes are read and zero-fill (or throw) the remainder, using the `stream.Read` return value it currently drops. Also stop poisoning freed frames with 0xFF, or move the 'read past EOF' assertion to check the actual byte count instead of `All(0)`.
duplicates.rationale: The MemoryCache half of [18]: readable-miss frames are published without Clear() (the write path does clear), so the design depends entirely on the factory overwriting all 8192 bytes.

duplicates.title: TransactionMonitor.ReleaseTransaction is not called from a finally, so a failure inside Rollback/Commit permanently leaks the transaction registration and the LockService read lock
duplicates.mech: In AutoTransaction's catch block, `transaction.Rollback()` and `_monitor.ReleaseTransaction(transaction)` are two sequential statements (lines 99-101). If Rollback() throws, the new exception replaces `throw;` and ReleaseTransaction never runs. ReleaseTransaction is the only place that (a) removes the transaction from TransactionRegistry, (b) calls _locker.ExitTransaction() to release the ReaderWriterLockSlim read lock taken by TransactionMonitor.GetTransaction, and (c) clears the ThreadLocal slot. TransactionService.Rollback() can throw: it calls ReturnNewPages() -> DiskService.WriteLogDisk() (an IOException on a full/failing disk) whenever _transPages.NewPages.Count > 0, and DiscardDirtyPages/DiscardCleanPages go through MemoryCache ENSURE checks which throw LiteException in release builds (ENSURE in Constants.cs is NOT [Conditional]). The same non-finally pattern exists in LiteEngine.Rollback() (line 68) and CommitAndReleaseTransaction (lines 110-112).
duplicates.fail: A batch insert that allocates new pages fails with a unique-index LiteException; AutoTransaction catches it, _state.Handle returns true, and transaction.Rollback() -> ReturnNewPages() -> WriteLogDisk() throws IOException because the volume is full. The read lock on LockService._transaction stays held by that thread for the engine's lifetime, so LockService.EnterExclusive/TryEnterExclusive can never succeed: every subsequent Checkpoint() throws LockTimeout, the log file grows without bound, and the final checkpoint on Dispose is silently skipped. The registry slot also leaks, so 100 such occurrences make every later operation fail with "Maximum number of transactions reached".
duplicates.fix: Put `_monitor.ReleaseTransaction(transaction)` in a finally around the Rollback()/Commit() call (in AutoTransaction, LiteEngine.Rollback and CommitAndReleaseTransaction) so the registration, thread slot and transaction read lock are released even when rollback/commit fails.
duplicates.rationale: Same missing try/finally around ReleaseTransaction as [2], reported from AutoTransaction's catch block.

duplicates.title: GetCollectionNames returns a lazy enumerator over the live header collection dictionary with no lock
duplicates.mech: HeaderPage.GetCollections() (Pages/HeaderPage.cs:219-225) is a yield-based iterator over _collections.GetElements(), i.e. over the plain Dictionary<string,BsonValue> backing the header's collections BsonDocument. GetCollectionNames wraps it in another deferred Select and hands it to the caller without materializing it and without taking lock(_header). Header mutation happens on other threads inside TransactionService.PersistDirtyPages under lock(_header): _transPages.OnCommit(_header) invokes the callbacks registered by CollectionService.Add (h.InsertCollection), Snapshot.DropCollection (h.DeleteCollection) and Collection.cs:82-85 (h.RenameCollection), all of which add/remove entries in that same dictionary. A reader enumerating concurrently is not synchronized with that writer. HeaderPage.Restore/LoadPage can also replace the _collections instance wholesale (HeaderPage.cs:147, 194-200), detaching the in-flight enumerator from the live state. The method also omits the _state.Validate() call that every other public engine entry point makes, so it silently returns stale names on a disposed engine.
duplicates.fail: Thread A: foreach (var n in engine.GetCollectionNames()) { /* any work per name */ }. Thread B concurrently runs engine.Insert("newCol", docs, BsonAutoId.Int32) on a collection that does not exist yet; at commit, OnCommit calls h.InsertCollection("newCol", pageID) which does _collections["newCol"] = pageID on the dictionary Thread A is enumerating. Thread A throws InvalidOperationException: 'Collection was modified; enumeration operation may not execute' out of a method on a type documented [ThreadSafe]. The same lazy-enumeration pattern is used by SysCols.cs:13, which is what LiteDatabase.GetCollectionNames() executes.
duplicates.fix: Materialize under the header lock: lock (_header) { return _header.GetCollections().Select(x => x.Key).ToArray(); } and add _state.Validate() at entry.
duplicates.rationale: Same unlocked lazy enumeration of HeaderPage._collections as [95], reported from GetCollectionNames; also notes the missing _state.Validate().

duplicates.title: SharedEngine never disposes its named Mutex and calls ReleaseMutex from whatever thread disposes the database
duplicates.mech: Dispose(bool) releases the mutex only when _engine != null and never calls _mutex.Dispose(), so the named-mutex WaitHandle is only reclaimed when its SafeWaitHandle is finalized (and on Windows SharedMutexFactory.WindowsMutex.Create additionally abandons the handle allocated by `new Mutex()` when it overwrites SafeWaitHandle). Worse, Mutex.ReleaseMutex() must be called on the owning thread: LiteDatabase.Dispose runs on whatever thread the caller uses, so disposing a SharedEngine that still has an open transaction from a different thread throws ApplicationException ("Object synchronization method was called from an unsynchronized block of code") out of Dispose - after _engine has already been disposed and nulled - and the mutex stays owned by the original thread.
duplicates.fail: Thread A: `db.BeginTrans(); col.Insert(x);` then an exception aborts A's work without Commit/Rollback. A DI container / finalizer thread B disposes the LiteDatabase: Dispose(true) sees _engine != null, disposes the engine, then `_mutex.ReleaseMutex()` throws ApplicationException out of the using-block, and the Global mutex remains owned, so all other processes stay blocked.
duplicates.fix: Guard the ReleaseMutex with try/catch (and only release acquisitions this thread actually made), and dispose _mutex in Dispose(true) so the OS handle is released deterministically.
duplicates.rationale: Same mutex thread-affinity/ownership problem as [160], plus the never-disposed WaitHandle and the abandoned handle from the Windows factory.

duplicates.title: EntityMapper.WaitForInitialization can touch a CancellationTokenSource that GetEntityMapper has already disposed, throwing ObjectDisposedException
duplicates.mech: GetEntityMapper (BsonMapper.GetEntityMapper.cs:27) creates the initialization CTS with `using var cts`, cancels it in `finally` (line 49) and then immediately disposes it, with no coordination with threads that may be waiting on it. WaitForInitialization first tests `IsCancellationRequested` (safe after Dispose) and only then dereferences `_initializationToken.WaitHandle`. `CancellationToken.WaitHandle` throws ObjectDisposedException once the owning source is disposed, so a waiter that passes the IsCancellationRequested test *before* the builder cancels, and reaches line 65 *after* the builder disposes, gets an ObjectDisposedException instead of a wait.
duplicates.fail: Two threads insert the first entity of type T concurrently. Thread A enters GetEntityMapper, publishes the empty shell into `_entities` (line 32) and starts BuildEntityMapper. Thread B hits the fast path (line 22), gets the same half-built mapper, and in SerializeObject (BsonMapper.Serialize.cs:261) calls WaitForInitialization: `IsCancellationRequested` is still false, and B is preempted between line 60 and line 65. Thread A finishes, runs `cts.Cancel()` then `cts.Dispose()`. Thread B resumes at line 65 and the `_initializationToken.WaitHandle` getter throws `ObjectDisposedException: The CancellationTokenSource has been disposed`, which escapes Insert/ToDocument as an unhandled exception (not even wrapped in a LiteException).
duplicates.fix: Don't dispose the CTS while its token is still observable from a cached EntityMapper — drop the `using` (let it be collected), or replace the token with a ManualResetEventSlim/TaskCompletionSource owned by the EntityMapper and signalled when the build completes; and guard the WaitHandle access with try/catch (ObjectDisposedException) treated as "already initialized".
duplicates.rationale: Same disposed-CancellationTokenSource race as [183], reported at the WaitHandle dereference.

duplicates.title: SortDisk.Dispose skips deletion of the temp sort file when the stream pool throws
duplicates.mech: Dispose() calls `_pool.Dispose()` and then `_factory.Delete()` with no try/finally. StreamPool.Dispose deliberately throws AggregateException when any pooled reader, the writer, or the factory fails to dispose, so the Delete() that removes the "<db>-tmp" file never runs. LiteEngine.Close swallows the exception via TryCatch, so nothing reports the leftover file. Dispose is also not idempotent-guarded (no _disposed flag), unlike the other services in this codebase.
duplicates.fail: A query spills an ORDER BY to the "<db>-tmp" sort file; at db.Dispose() the temp FileStream fails to close (e.g. IOException while flushing on a full volume). StreamPool.Dispose throws, `_factory.Delete()` is skipped, and the multi-megabyte "<db>-tmp" file is left on disk indefinitely with no error surfaced to the caller.
duplicates.fix: Wrap the pool disposal in try/finally (or collect errors like DiskService.Dispose does) so _factory.Delete() always runs, and add an Interlocked _disposed guard.
duplicates.rationale: Same missing try/finally around the temp-file delete as [76].

duplicates.title: BufferSlice.ReadCString mixes absolute array positions with slice-relative indices and reads outside the slice
duplicates.mech: The method conflates three different coordinate systems. `length = buffer.Count - buffer.Offset - offset` subtracts the slice's start position from the slice's LENGTH, which is meaningless. The scan starts at `i = offset + buffer.Offset` (an absolute array position) but dereferences `buffer[i]`, and BufferSlice's indexer is slice-relative (`Array[Offset + index]`, BufferSlice.cs:44) - so Offset is applied twice and the scan actually inspects Array[2*Offset + offset ...]. The loop bound `i < buffer.Count` compares that Offset-inflated index against the slice length. Everything only happens to be correct when buffer.Offset == 0. Page buffers are carved out of one shared byte[] per cache segment (`new byte[PAGE_SIZE * segmentSize]`, LiteDB/Engine/Disk/PageFramePool.cs:198), so for Offset > 0 the scan reads bytes belonging to other page segments/pages rather than the slice's own content, and the returned `length` out-parameter (used by callers to advance) is wrong. If buffer.Offset > buffer.Count the computed length is negative and Encoding.UTF8.GetString(..., length - 1) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
duplicates.fail: Call ReadCString(offset: 0) on a segment slice with Offset = 100, Count = 200 holding "ab\0": length is initialised to 200-100-0 = 100, the scan probes Array[200..299] (a different page's bytes) instead of Array[100..199], and the method returns Encoding.UTF8.GetString(Array, 100, 99) - 99 bytes of unrelated page content - or a truncated string plus a bogus `length` if a 0x00 happens to appear in the foreign region. The defect is latent today: grep shows no caller of this overload (the ReadCString calls elsewhere resolve to BufferReader.ReadCString), so it is reachable only by a future caller.
duplicates.fix: Work entirely in slice-relative coordinates: `length = buffer.Count - offset; for (var i = offset; i < buffer.Count; i++) if (buffer[i] == 0) { length = i - offset + 1; break; }` - or delete the unused overload.
duplicates.rationale: Same dead ReadCString overload as [29].

duplicates.title: Database password is stretched with PBKDF2 defaults (1000 iterations, HMAC-SHA1), making offline password recovery cheap
duplicates.mech: `new Rfc2898DeriveBytes(password, salt)` selects the constructor defaults: IterationCount = 1000 and HashAlgorithm = SHA-1. The 32-byte key and 16-byte IV for the whole file come from that single derivation. The 16-byte salt is random per file (NewSalt, line 226) so rainbow tables are prevented, but 1000 iterations of HMAC-SHA1 is roughly three orders of magnitude below current guidance (OWASP: >=1.3M for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1), and the file itself contains a free verifier - 32 bytes of encrypted 0x01 at offset 32 - so a candidate password can be tested with one PBKDF2 call plus one AES block.
duplicates.fail: An attacker obtains a stolen encrypted .db file. Each password guess costs 1000 HMAC-SHA1 operations plus a single AES-ECB block decrypt of bytes 32..47, checked against 0x01 repeated. Commodity GPU hardware performs on the order of 10^7 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1(1000) guesses per second, so an 8-character human-chosen password is recovered in minutes to hours - an attack that a modern iteration count would push to years.
duplicates.fix: Use the explicit overload `new Rfc2898DeriveBytes(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256)` with a high iteration count, and persist the iteration count/algorithm in the file header so existing files stay readable and the parameters can be raised over time.
duplicates.rationale: Same PBKDF2 defaults as [58].

duplicates.title: AesStream derives its blank-page sentinel from an ArrayPool buffer that is never zeroed, so the sentinel can be wrong
duplicates.mech: `msBuffer = _bufferPool.Rent(16)` (line 65) returns a buffer from the process-wide ArrayPool<byte>.Shared, which explicitly does NOT guarantee zeroed contents. The constructor then wraps that buffer in a MemoryStream and decrypts it into `_decryptedZeroes` (lines 151-155) with the intent of caching decrypt(16 zero bytes). Nothing clears msBuffer first. LiteDB's own call sites all Return(..., clearArray: true), but ArrayPool<byte>.Shared is shared with every other component in the host process (ASP.NET Core, System.Text.Json, third-party libraries), none of which is obliged to clear 16-byte buffers on return. If the rented buffer contains residue, `_decryptedZeroes` holds decrypt(residue) and the unsafe IsBlank() check (line 256) compares page data against the wrong 16 bytes.
duplicates.fail: A web application hosting LiteDB has previously rented and returned a dirty 16-byte array to ArrayPool<byte>.Shared. It then opens an encrypted database whose log contains a page that was never written (all-zero ciphertext - the exact condition the code comments say IsBlank exists to handle). _decryptedZeroes is decrypt(residue) rather than decrypt(zeroes), so IsBlank() returns false, Read() hands the caller a page of repeated garbage instead of zeroing it, and WalIndexService.RestoreIndex/CheckpointInternal - which the comment says relies on blank pages being skipped - parses the garbage as a page header and throws instead of skipping, so the database fails to open.
duplicates.fix: Either `Array.Clear(msBuffer, 0, 16)` before wrapping it, or simply use a 16-byte stack/local array (`new byte[16]`) - the allocation is negligible and removes the dependency on unspecified pool behaviour.
duplicates.rationale: Same unzeroed ArrayPool sentinel as [54].

refuted.title: A transient failure creating the log writer is cached by Lazy<Stream> forever, permanently disabling all writes
refuted.why:
The quoted code and line are accurate: DiskService.cs:176 is `var stream = _writer.Value;` inside WriteLogDisk, _writer is `_logPool.Writer` (DiskService.cs:47), and StreamPool.cs:27 builds it as `new Lazy<Stream>(() => this.CreateWriter(appendOnly), true)`, i.e. ExecutionAndPublication, which does cache initializer exceptions. themes:
Fourteen patterns explain most of the 203 findings; fixing the pattern is usually cheaper than fixing the instances.

1. ENSURE is not [Conditional], so internal invariant checks throw LiteException(INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE) in release builds, and EngineState.Handle escalates that to LiteEngine.Close + MarkAsInvalidState. This converts ~a dozen assertion sites into whole-engine shutdowns that stamp a healthy data file as invalid: [3] [6] [19] [20] [24] [33] [39] [42] [55] [93]. Mitigating factor verified: EngineSettings.AutoRebuild defaults to false, and LiteEngine.Open ignores the marker unless AutoRebuild is set, which caps the destructive tail of these.

2. The single-argument BsonValue.CompareTo hardcodes Collation.Binary while the rest of the engine threads the configured collation, so index scans, relational operators, aggregates and nested values disagree with =, ORDER BY and index seeks: [64] [66] [103] [104] [120]. Related contract breaks in the same type: [101] (CompareTo is not antisymmetric for documents with disjoint keys - verified), [105] (Equals/GetHashCode disagree), [177] (Collation's IEqualityComparer).

3. Index/sort-key framing has three readers with incompatible rules - ExtendedLengthHelper's 6-bit type mask, BufferReader.ReadIndexKey's unmasked type plus 8-bit length, and BufferSliceExtensions.ReadIndexKey's extended-length decode. Groups: [25]/[70] (canonical [25]), [26]/[172] (canonical [172]), [31]/[72] (canonical [72]).

4. The vector feature was grafted onto B-tree assumptions and produces the single largest defect cluster: the MAX_INDEX_LENGTH=1400 free-list threshold ([6]/[33]/[42], canonical [42]), BsonType.Vector=100 overflowing the 6-bit mask ([26]/[172]), the tail-sentinel comparison ([41]), VECTOR_SIM's Null-sorts-lowest semantics in the unindexed fallback ([48] [49]), external payloads masquerading as document start blocks ([44]), unvalidated metric/neighbour counts ([46] [47]), graph orphaning ([43]) and O(N^2) upsert ([45]). Existing tests only cover 2/3/6/8/32 dimensions plus one >1996 case, leaving the entire 307..1996 window - every real embedding size - untested.

5. Free-page reclamation is opportunistic rather than invariant-driven, so several paths silently orphan pages and grow the file without bound: [7] (safepoint destroys the commit-time link), [10] (DropCollection overwrites the chain), [40]/[78] (DropIndex never returns pages).

6. Lock and transaction release is written as sequential statements rather than try/finally, and the engine read lock is thread-affine while the release paths are not: [2]/[182], [4], [9], [133], [160]/[186], [162]. The consequence is always the same shape - a leaked read lock disables every checkpoint for the process lifetime and the log grows unbounded.

7. Rebuild/Recovery trusts a caller-supplied RebuildOptions with no fallback to engine settings and swallows loader failures. Verified: LiteDatabase.Rebuild(options=null) manufactures a null-password, null-collation option object, and FileReaderV8.HandleError rethrows only IOException. Group: [11]/[164] (canonical [11]), plus [13] [15] [16] [85] [165] [170] [171]. RebuildService also never copies the COLLATION pragma.

8. SharedEngine's cross-process mutex is acquired unconditionally, released conditionally, thread-affine, and never disposed: [157]/[180] (canonical [157]), [158]/[181] (canonical [158]), [159], [160]/[186] (canonical [160]), [161], [162], [163]. Any one of these leaves a Global mutex owned forever, which wedges the database file for every other process.

9. The hand-rolled SqlLike matcher is wrong in four independent ways plus its prefix helper; one rewrite fixes all of them. I confirmed each by re-implementing the function verbatim and sweeping all patterns of length <=5 over {a,b,%,_} against inputs of length <=4: 688 non-terminating cases and 136 negative-index cases ([173]), 92 false positives from the stale pattern char ([174]), 1364 false negatives from "%_" ([176]), and SqlLikeStartsWith("abc_") returning hasMore=false ([175]). Because StringResolver maps StartsWith/Contains/EndsWith onto LIKE ([150], which additionally passes user wildcards through unescaped), this is the highest-exposure correctness cluster in the codebase.

10. Unchecked narrowing and unvalidated framework-call arguments across the expression and engine API layers: [79]/[194], [100], [117]/[188], [118], [119], [121]/[190], [123]/[191]/[192], [124]/[193], [169], [171], [189]. The project sets no CheckForOverflowUnderflow, so every (int)/(byte) cast in this list wraps silently.

11. All three recursive-descent parsers (JSON, expression, tokenizer) lack a depth limit, and .NET makes StackOverflowException uncatchable, so untrusted text terminates the host process: [125]/[197] (canonical [125]), [111], [112]; [108] is the same hazard reached through a self-referencing document.

12. Untrusted on-disk bytes drive allocations, loop bounds and slice offsets with no validation, no cycle detection and no per-page checksum: [27] [28] [30] [34] [35] [38] [47] [86] [87] [88] [89] [90] [91] [92] [195]. Because PageFramePool allocates one array per 8- or 128-page segment, several of these read or write across page boundaries inside the shared buffer.

13. $system collections lazily enumerate other threads' live containers without the header lock that writers take: [80]/[95] (canonical [95]), [94], [96], and [93] for the disposed-snapshot variant.

14. Culture-sensitive ToUpper/ToLower/ToString on paths that must be invariant: [53] [131] [147] [148] [167] [178]. The codebase already uses ToUpperInvariant and an invariant NumberFormat elsewhere, so each of these is an inconsistency rather than a design choice.

Cross-tier note on severity: I raised [157]/[180] to critical (permanent cross-process wedge per the rubric) and [173] to critical (an unbounded loop inside an open read transaction wedges checkpoints and Dispose). I lowered [3] and [93] from "destroys the database" reasoning to high once AutoRebuild's false default was confirmed, and lowered the FileReaderV7 cluster ([87] [89] [90] [91] [195]) to medium/low because that reader is reachable only through Upgrade=true or a v4 file in RebuildService.

Cheapest high-leverage fixes, in order: (a) FlushToDisk on the log write path [12]; (b) seed RebuildOptions from _settings [11]/[164]; (c) rethrow non-IOException from FileReaderV8.Open or refuse to install an empty rebuild [85]; (d) rewrite SqlLike/SqlLikeStartsWith [173]-[176]; (e) reorder the operator reduction to respect equal precedence [110]; (f) add the `right != index.Tail` guard in IndexService.Find [39]/[41]; (g) wrap ReleaseMutex/ReleaseTransaction in try/finally and make the shared mutex acquisition symmetric [2] [157] [158].
gaps:
Judging by where the 203 findings cluster, the audit over-sampled expression/parser/mapper surface area and under-sampled the write path and concurrency.

Under-covered:
- Write path serialization. Every serializer finding is on a reader (BufferReader, BufferSliceExtensions.Read*, BsonElementReader). BufferWriter, WriteElement, WriteCString, the ObjectId/Guid/Decimal/DateTime encoders and BasePage.Update/Insert byte layout are essentially unexamined, yet finding [34] shows the write side is where a bad slice becomes on-disk corruption.
- WAL/checkpoint concurrency. Only [1] and [17] touch it, and [17] is self-admittedly unproven. There is nothing on RestoreIndex's version/position ordering, _currentReadVersion visibility, concurrent TryCheckpoint vs commit, or the disk writer queue's ordering guarantees - which is exactly the area the one confirmed critical durability bug ([12]) lives in.
- MemoryCache/PageFramePool internals. [23] and [24] are incidental; the reclaimer's eviction policy, ShareCounter transitions, segment growth under pressure and the Writable->Readable handoff are unaudited despite every page in the engine passing through them.
- Core DML semantics. No findings on Update/Upsert/DeleteMany correctness, multikey index maintenance (add/remove of the per-document node chain), or Include/DbRef resolution beyond [140] and [156]. IndexService.AddNode/DeleteSingleNode link maintenance is only reached indirectly via [37] and [39].
- SQL parser breadth. Coverage is REBUILD, LIMIT/OFFSET, the transaction verbs and keyword casing. UPDATE/INSERT/SELECT projection, aggregate and INTO parsing, and the JSON-document literal path, are untouched.
- Cross-process file sharing outside SharedEngine: FileStreamFactory's FileShare flags, byte-range locking, and what two direct-mode processes on one file actually do.
- Encryption beyond AesStream's constructor: the Write path, page-boundary alignment, and what happens when a password is added to an existing file.

Distribution artifacts to be aware of:
- Roughly 40 of the 203 entries are duplicates or facets (I marked 33 with duplicate_of), heavily concentrated in the crosscut-* areas, which were evidently run over ground the per-area passes had already covered. The true distinct-defect count is closer to 170.
- The vector module produced ~15 distinct defects, several of which make the feature unusable at real embedding sizes; that ratio suggests the module shipped with little adversarial review, and the remaining vector code (Search.cs, PruneNeighbors, level sampling) probably still hides more.
- Several findings are stated with explicit uncertainty ([8] [17] [26] [31] [41] [43] [141] [163]); of those I flagged six as shaky. Nothing in the set was verified by actually running the code - I could confirm SqlLike and the operator-precedence reduction only by re-implementing them outside the repo - so a maintainer should expect a reproduction step to be the first task on any item ranked below ~40.

Read end to end: LiteDB/Engine/Services/TransactionService.cs, TransactionMonitor.cs, LockService.cs, LiteDB/Engine/Engine/Transaction.cs. Followed call chains into (read-only) TransactionRegistry.cs, TransactionPageCleanup.cs, CollectionLock.cs, Structures/TransactionPages.cs, Services/SnapShot.cs, Services/WalIndexService.cs, Disk/DiskService.cs, Disk/DiskReader.cs, Disk/MemoryCache.cs, Disk/CacheReclaimer.cs, Pages/BasePage.cs, EngineState.cs, LiteEngine.cs, Query/QueryExecutor.cs, Engine/Insert.cs, Engine/Update.cs, Engine/Rebuild.cs, Utils/Constants.cs, Utils/TryCatch.cs, Client/Database/Collections/Find.cs, Client/Database/LiteQueryable.cs. Key confirmed facts used above: ENSURE is not [Conditional] (Constants.cs:137) so it throws in release builds as LiteException.INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE, which EngineState.Handle escalates to LiteEngine.Close(ex) + DiskService.MarkAsInvalidState(); Snapshot.Dispose() for a write snapshot releases the collection Monitor but not its page buffers; LiteCollection.Find is lazy.

Could not verify by execution: no dotnet/mono/msbuild toolchain is available in this container, so none of the scenarios were reproduced - all findings are static traces. Finding 1 (duplicate transactionID) and finding 4 (cross-thread read-lock leak) are the two whose *trigger* I could not pin down empirically: finding 1 needs a Checkpoint() to land in the window between NextTransactionID() and EnterTransaction() plus enough subsequent commits to re-issue the same ID, and finding 4 depends on the enumerator being disposed on a different thread than the one that called ExecuteQuery (realistic under async/await continuations but I did not instrument it); both are marked medium confidence for that reason.

Candidates examined and deliberately discarded as unproven: (a) the Read->Write snapshot replacement leaking write-snapshot page buffers - reachable only when the replaced snapshot is write-mode with CollectionPage == null, which cannot have accumulated local pages; (b) a partially-failed Commit() leaving _state == Active so a following Rollback() returns just-committed pages to the free list (mechanism is real - _state = Committed is set only at TransactionService.cs:282, after the snapshot-dispose loop - but I could not prove any realistic exception source between ConfirmTransaction and that assignment); (c) TransactionRegistry.Add's unbounded yield-free spin loop and its reserve-before-publish spurious "Maximum number of transactions reached" - low impact and TransactionRegistry.cs is outside the reporting scope; (d) ENSURE(_slot.Value == transaction) inside ReleaseTransaction's finally (TransactionMonitor.cs:131) escalating an in-memory bookkeeping mismatch to an engine-killing INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE and skipping `_slot.Value = null` / TrimToLimit - real hazard but I found no reachable way to make the predicate false; (e) managed-thread-ID reuse making `alreadyLock` (TransactionMonitor.cs:60) skip EnterTransaction for a fresh thread - traced through and the abandoned entry's read lock is still counted, so there is no exclusivity bypass, only the lock leak already covered by finding 4; (f) TransactionMonitor.Dispose() releasing page buffers of transactions that other threads are actively using, and WalIndexService.Checkpoint/TryCheckpoint reading _confirmTransactions.Count without _indexLock - both real but engine-shutdown-only / outside the assigned files.

Not covered: the DiskService log-durability question (WriteLogDisk uses stream.Flush(), not FlushToDisk, so a confirm page can reach disk ahead of earlier in-place slot overwrites) and the in-place WAL slot-reuse optimisation at DiskService.cs:191-199 - both belong to the disk/WAL area and should be audited there.

To prove or refute candidates I also read: Pages/BasePage.cs (ownership/epoch/OwnsBuffer/TakeBuffer, Insert/Delete/Update dirty flags, MarkAsEmtpy, ReadPage/CreatePage dispatch), Pages/CollectionPage.cs (FreeDataPageList is a live uint[] so `ref ...[slot]` is correct; _indexes/_vectorIndexes are in-memory so reading them after MarkAsEmtpy is safe; UpdateBuffer early-returns for Empty), Pages/DataPage.cs + IndexPage.cs + VectorIndexPage.cs (free-slot thresholds), Services/TransactionService.cs (Safepoint, PersistDirtyPages, Commit, Rollback, ReturnNewPages, Dispose), Services/TransactionPageCleanup.cs, Services/CollectionService.cs, Services/LockService.cs, Services/TransactionMonitor.cs (CheckSafepoint, GetThreadTransaction), Disk/MemoryCache.cs, Disk/DiskReader.cs, Disk/DiskService.WriteLogDisk, Structures/TransactionPages.cs, Structures/IndexNode.cs + VectorIndexNode.cs + VectorIndexMetadata.cs, Services/IndexService.cs (CreateIndex/AddNode/FindAll/DropIndex), Services/VectorIndexService.cs (Insert/Drop), Engine/Collection.cs, Engine/Delete.cs, Engine/Transaction.cs (AutoTransaction), Query/QueryExecutor.cs, SystemCollections/SysPageList.cs, Utils/Constants.cs (ENSURE is NOT [Conditional] — it throws in Release; DEBUG() is DEBUG-only).

Candidates I investigated and DISCARDED as unprovable or guarded: (1) stale BasePage left in _localPages by NewPage<CollectionPage> — the constructor's `_localPages.Remove(_collectionPage.PageID)` (line 90) removes it and the catch block re-keys the same pageID, so no double-discard; (2) double-Release of read-snapshot buffers between TransactionPageCleanup and Snapshot.Dispose — TransactionService.Dispose only runs cleanup when _state == Active and then sets Disposed, and Commit/Rollback ENSURE Active, so no second release path; (3) NewPage inside a Read-mode snapshot (would leak a dirty page GetWritablePages never yields) — unreachable: every CreateSnapshot(LockMode.Read, ...) call site passes addIfNotExists=false; (4) InvalidCastException from RemoveFreeList's `GetPage<BasePage>(page.NextPageID)` ENSURE — the next page was already loaded as T a few lines earlier, so it is only an upcast; (5) `FreeBytes > bytesLength` in GetFreeIndexPage — index nodes max out at 1355 bytes vs the 1400 threshold, so it holds; (6) uint overflow in the LimitSize check — `_header.LastPageID + 1` promotes to long; (7) use-after-Clear of a page held across a safepoint — IndexService.FindAll deliberately reads the next address before yielding, and Snapshot.Clear refreshes only the deliberately-retained collection page's epoch; (8) lock-order inversion between lock(_header) in NewPage and MemoryCache._sync — no path holds _sync and then takes _header.

Gaps a follow-up should cover: I did not run or build anything (read-only task), so finding #1's exact failing insert ordinal per dimension count is computed from FreeBytes/FooterSize arithmetic rather than observed; a 10-line xunit test (1536-dim vector index, two inserts) would confirm it in seconds. I also did not audit DataService.cs's own free-list bookkeeping (whether AddOrRemoveFreeDataList is called on every mutation path), nor VectorIndexService.ClearTree/StoreVector page accounting, nor the WAL recovery path's treatment of orphaned Empty pages — the latter is the natural follow-up for finding #2 (does Rebuild reclaim them?).

Candidates I investigated and DISCARDED as unprovable or non-defects:
- v8 -> v9 vector-format downgrade via replay/rollback/checkpoint. `HeaderPage.EnsureVersion` is monotonic (Math.Max), `LoadPage` re-maxes on load, `Restore(savepoint)` re-applies `EnsureVersion(_fileVersion)`, `RestoreIndex` captures the pre-copy `fileVersion` and re-applies it after the log header overwrite, and `DiskService.PreserveFileVersion` raises the byte on every header write to both files. `PromoteVectorFormat` fsyncs the data header before any vector byte can reach the WAL, so a v9 log header can never coexist with a v8 data header. `_disk.FileVersion` not being refreshed after `RestoreIndex` is therefore latent-only; I could not construct a reachable downgrade.
- Partially written WAL tail. `ReadFull` would hand out a page padded with the previous page's bytes on a short read, but `FileStreamFactory.GetLength()`/`StreamFactory.GetLength()` truncate any non-PAGE_SIZE-aligned file before the length is ever published, and `ENSURE(bytesRead == PAGE_SIZE)` is live in release builds. Not reachable.
- Log-order vs commit-order in `RestoreIndex` and `CheckpointInternal`, including the unconfirmed-slot-reuse optimisation in `WriteLogDisk` and the "final safepoint" duplicate-confirm append in `PersistDirtyPages`. I walked several interleavings (two concurrent transactions on different collections; a page written twice in one transaction; abandoned-transaction slots). In every case the backwards scan in `GetPageIndex` and the log-order overwrite in `WriteDataDisk` pick the newest image. No defect proven.
- Checkpoint concurrent with readers. `EnterExclusive`/`TryEnterExclusive` correctly serialise against the per-transaction read lock, and `MemoryCache.Invalidate`'s pinned/loading assertions hold because `Snapshot.Dispose`/`Commit` release every frame. The `mustExit == false` branches in both lock helpers are dead code today (checkpoint is the only `EnterExclusive` caller).
- Unsynchronised `_confirmTransactions.Count` read at WalIndexService.cs:270/293. Real (HashSet is not thread-safe) but `Count` is a single int field; worst case is a skipped or redundant checkpoint attempt that is then re-validated under the exclusive lock. Benign, not reported.
- `page 0` entering `_index` during `RestoreIndex` (the `written` callback filters pageID 0 but `RestoreIndex` does not). Harmless because `Snapshot.GetPage(0)` short-circuits to the in-memory `_header` and never consults the WAL index.

Gaps a follow-up should cover:
- I did not build or execute anything (read-only task), so all findings are static traces. The `:memory:` Rebuild finding and the plaintext-Rebuild finding are both cheap to confirm with a 10-line test; worth doing before fixing.
- The missing log fsync (finding 2) is anchored in DiskService.cs, outside my assigned report paths, but it is the direct answer to the durability lens and has no owner inside WalIndexService. Whoever owns the disk layer should confirm whether the async `DiskWriterQueue` this replaced fsynced (upstream LiteDB v5 did) - git history in this fork does not contain that file.
- `TransactionMonitor.Dispose()` disposes transactions belonging to other threads without exiting their `_transaction` read lock and while those threads may still be using the pages (`TransactionPageCleanup.Release` runs with `releaseLock: false` cross-thread). That looks like a real use-after-free / lock-leak pair, but it is in TransactionMonitor/TransactionService, outside my scope, and I did not finish proving the interleaving. It also silently suppresses the shutdown checkpoint in `LiteEngine.Close()` (TryCheckpoint sees `CurrentReadCount > 0`). Recommend assigning it explicitly.
- `RebuildService.Rebuild`'s three-step `File.Move` sequence is not atomic: a crash or a locked file between `File.Move(_settings.Filename, backupFilename)` and `File.Move(tempFilename, _settings.Filename)` leaves no file at the database path (data recoverable only from `-backup`), and the second move has no retry wrapper unlike the first. Also `-temp` files are left behind when a rebuild throws. Not reported because RebuildService.cs is outside my report scope; belongs to whoever owns that file.

Scope note: LiteDB/Engine/Disk/DiskWriterQueue.cs does not exist in this fork — the background writer queue has been replaced by the synchronous DiskService.WriteLogDisk, so the 'writer queue exception propagation / failed background write never reported' lens has no target: every log write now happens on the committing thread inside lock(stream) and its exceptions propagate to the caller (TransactionService.PersistDirtyPages). I read DiskService.cs, DiskService.FileVersion.cs and DiskReader.cs end to end, plus everything needed to prove or kill candidates: StreamPool.cs, IStreamFactory.cs, FileStreamFactory.cs, StreamFactory.cs, ConcurrentStream.cs, NonClosingStream.cs, TempStream.cs, AesStream.cs, StreamExtensions.cs, MemoryCache.cs, SharedPageReads.cs, PageBuffer.cs/BufferSlice.cs, Constants.cs, FileHelper.cs/IOExceptionExtensions.cs, EngineSettings.cs, LiteEngine.cs (open/close), TransactionService.cs (persist/commit/rollback), TransactionMonitor.Dispose, WalIndexService.cs and Snapshot.ReadPage. Git log/blame checked for the flush and read regions.

Candidates I deliberately DISCARDED after tracing:
- WAL commit is never fsynced (DiskService.cs:244 uses stream.Flush(), and no FlushToDisk exists on the log path anywhere) — this is a documented, deliberate design decision, not a defect: docs/vector-query-compatibility.md:174 ('WAL commit still uses parameterless Flush() in WriteLogDisk; the change does not add fsync to every commit') and docs/memory-management-proposal.md:83. Worth flagging to the maintainers as a durability property (an acked commit is lost on power loss), but I did not report it as a bug.
- WriteLogDisk failure/rollback path (DiskService.cs:222-242): I walked each throw point (ENSURE, stream.Length, PreserveFileVersion, stream.Write, MoveToReadable, the written callback). Frame ownership and the _logLength/stream.Length reservations reconcile correctly in every case, including the AesStream +PAGE_SIZE offset in Length/SetLength; earlier pages of a failed batch stay in the log but are unconfirmed, so recovery ignores them.
- The new unconfirmed-slot reuse branch (DiskService.cs:194-199) plus _cache.Invalidate: MemoryCache.EvictLocked ENSUREs the frame is Readable with ShareCounter==0, which would throw inside a commit if any reader still pinned that log position. I could not construct a reachable pinner: unconfirmed slots are visible only through the owning transaction's _transPages.DirtyPages, write snapshots take writable copies and release the readable pin immediately (MemoryCache.cs:172-203), SharedPageReads holds hints not pins, and a same-collection read snapshot is disposed when upgraded to write. Reported nothing, but this invariant is thinner than the code comment suggests and is worth a targeted stress test (read snapshot on collection A + write snapshot on collection B in one transaction, multiple safepoints).
- Duplicate same-version WAL slots after reuse (a stale copy of a page at its reused low position plus the appended confirmed copy): benign, because WalIndexService.GetPageIndex scans the slot list backwards (WalIndexService.cs:118-137) and CheckpointInternal applies pages in file order, so the later/higher position wins in both paths.
- Unsynchronised use of the data writer in WriteDataDisk (DiskService.cs:345) and MarkAsInvalidState (DiskService.cs:273) while PromoteVectorFormat takes lock(stream) on the same stream: checkpoint holds the engine exclusive lock and PromoteVectorFormat runs under the header lock inside a write transaction, so the documented exclusion holds for those two. The one gap I could not prove is MarkAsInvalidState during Close(ex): TransactionMonitor.Dispose does not wait for threads already inside the engine, so in principle its read/modify/write of page 0 could interleave with another thread's checkpoint write on the same stream. I could not establish a concrete interleaving, so I left it unreported.
- Exceptions raised inside WriteLogDisk's catch block (SetLength/TrimCapacity/DiscardPage) would mask the original write error; plausible but I could not show a realistic case where the rollback operations themselves fail.
- StreamPool Rent/Return/Dispose races, DiskService constructor cleanup (double-dispose is idempotent per IStreamFactory's contract), DiskReader.Dispose ordering, and ReadFull's iterator-scoped Rent/Return all checked and found sound."

Candidates I chased and DISCARDED as provably safe (documenting so a follow-up does not redo them):
- SharedPageReads lock-free pin (TryPin/TryReleaseShared) vs the monitor-protected accounting. Verified every interleaving: TryPin only CASes when the observed count is > 0, and a value > 0 is only ever held by a Readable+pinned frame (Free/Loading set 0, Writable sets -1), so ABA reuse cannot hand out an unpinned/recycled frame; the post-CAS Position/Origin identity check plus Release on mismatch keeps it net-zero. TryReleaseShared never takes 1 -> 0, so the idle transition always happens under _sync. _pinnedPages/_idleReadablePages/segment.Busy balance across all six transition sites (loader publication, PublishWritableLocked pinned/unpinned, PinLocked, Release, TransitionToFreeLocked).
- SharedPageReads hint array cannot retain a frame from a released segment: Remember/Forget always use the same slot (Position is immutable while Readable), Forget runs under _sync before Position is reset, and its CAS comparand means a lost race implies the slot holds a different frame.
- CacheReclaimer.ClockUntilVictimLocked cannot fail to find a victim when _idleReadablePages > 0 (2*TotalPages steps == exactly two full cycles from any start; the idle set and Referenced bits are frozen because nothing outside _sync can move a frame pinned->idle, and TryPin only writes Referenced for frames the clock already skips). So AcquireFrameLocked cannot spin forever or trip its ENSURE.
- CacheReclaimer.TrimToLimit terminates (ReleasableSegments only contains Busy==0 segments, so a chosen candidate always becomes fully free, and the evicted/before guard breaks).
- PageFramePool free-list, bucket, _fullyFreeSegments and clock-cursor bookkeeping; NextClockFrameLocked cannot index out of range (removal always resets the cursor to 0,0).

Invariants verified as CORRECT (candidates discarded):
- The core accounting invariant NextFreePosition == PAGE_HEADER_SIZE + UsedBytes + FragmentedBytes holds through every branch of Insert/Delete/Update(shrink)/Update(grow)/Defrag; the ENSURE at BasePage.cs:352 is an exact restatement of it.
- Defrag is only ever entered with FragmentedBytes > 0 (proved: for isNewInsert=false, continuousBlocks == FreeBytes >= bytesLength by the caller guard; for isNewInsert=true, continuousBlocks >= bytesLength whenever Frag == 0), so its ENSURE cannot fire in normal operation. emptyLength can never be negative in a consistent page.
- DataService.Update's `bytesToCopy = Math.Min(bytesLeft, dataPage.FreeBytes + currentBlock.Buffer.Count)` exactly saturates BasePage.Update's grow-path budget (FreeBytes + oldLength), so the InvalidFreeSpacePage throw at BasePage.cs:346 is unreachable from the engine — the partial-state hazard in Update's grow path (slot cleared + ItemsCount decremented before the insert) is not provably triggerable, so I did not report it. Note line 344-347's throw is dead code: the ENSURE at 340 fires first with a different exception.
- FreeBytes returning 0 at ItemsCount == 255 is handled: DataPage.FreeIndexSlot(0) = 4, and GetFreeDataPage's search never starts above slot 3, so full pages are not re-offered.
- IndexPage.FreeIndexSlot's 1400-byte threshold is sound (max index node = 12 + 320 + 1023 = 1355 < 1400); the identical code in VectorIndexPage is not (finding 1).
- CollectionPage's P_INDEXES_COUNT check and GetSerializedLength match CollectionIndex.UpdateBuffer/GetLength byte-for-byte; writes end at 8191 at worst. HeaderPage's COLLECTIONS_SIZE = 8000 exactly reaches PAGE_SIZE from P_COLLECTIONS = 192 (the "192-8159 (8064 bytes)" comment is stale but the code is right). RenameCollection is space-checked by CollectionService.CheckName.
- BsonDocument and LockService both use StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, so collection-name casing is consistent; header mutation is serialized by lock(_header) in Commit/ReturnNewPages/NewPage (Safepoint's PersistDirtyPages(false) touches no header field).
- New page buffers are fully zeroed (MemoryCache.NewPage -> page.Clear() over all PAGE_SIZE bytes; MarkAsEmtpy clears 32..8191), so the "recycled dirty frame" variant of finding 3 is not reachable without an externally corrupted file.

Lenses walked and found clean (with the reasoning that discarded the candidates):
- Skip-list linking/unlinking at all levels (AddNode 107-155, DeleteSingleNode 277-298): level arrays are always indexed below Levels because a node reached via a level-L pointer necessarily has Levels > L; head/tail keep 32 levels; deleting the only node at a level correctly restores head<->tail links. AddNode's `last` is reloaded (line 163) to survive a same-page defrag, and the pre-reload `ENSURE(last.NextNode == Empty)` reads an in-memory field, so it is safe; DeleteList/EnsureIndex both leave `last.NextNode` Empty as required.
- Overflow/extend chains and partially-applied multi-page updates (DataService 83-159): I tried hard to build a case where two blocks of one document share a page so that a mid-update Defrag would invalidate an earlier `lastBlock`/yielded BufferSlice. It is unreachable: every non-final block is filled to exactly MAX_DATA_BYTES_PER_PAGE (Insert) or to FreeBytes+oldLen (Update), leaving the page with 0-6 free bytes, i.e. free-list slot 4, which GetFreeDataPage never scans (startSlot maxes at 3). Also verified the `bytesToCopy = FreeBytes + Buffer.Count` arithmetic exactly matches what BasePage.Update/InternalInsert require, and that BufferWriter.Consume() always drains the iterator so the trailing-block deletion (lines 141-148) cannot be skipped.
- Free-page bucket transitions: verified the NextFreePosition == 32 + UsedBytes + FragmentedBytes invariant across Insert/Delete/Update(shrink+grow)/Defrag/empty-reset, that GetMinimumIndexSlot always picks a bucket whose guaranteed free space exceeds the request, that index pages in bucket 0 always have >= MAX_INDEX_LENGTH(1400) free while the largest possible node is 12+320+1025 = 1357 bytes, and that PageListSlot never diverges from the list a page is actually in on any live path.
- Index key size limits: GetKeyLength/WriteIndexKey/ReadIndexKey agree for every type (strings/binaries use ExtendedLengthHelper's 10-bit length, documents/arrays carry their own BSON length prefix, vectors a ushort count), and MAX_INDEX_KEY_LENGTH(1023) keeps every node under MAX_INDEX_LENGTH.
- Duplicate keys: detection at level 0 is complete (leftNode always ends with key <= new key, and equal keys form a contiguous run to its right). The node is written into the page before the IndexDuplicateKey throw and the free-list fix-up at line 168 is skipped, but AutoTransaction -> EngineState.Handle rolls back the entire transaction (explicit transactions included), so no orphan node or stale PageListSlot survives — discarded.
- Dangling references on delete: DeleteAll/DeleteList/DataService.Delete all read the `NextNode`/`NextBlock` pointer from the in-memory structure before the page is mutated, and a page whose last item is removed cannot host the next element of the chain, so MarkAsEmtpy's buffer clear is never reached through a live pointer.

Lenses worked and found SOUND (candidates deliberately discarded):
- SortService.Sort() merge loop: verified `current` can never be EOF at the top of an iteration, and the duplicate-key fast path (`current?.Current.Key == lastKey`) is safe. The `diff == diffOrder` exact-+/-1 comparison is safe because every BsonValue.CompareTo leaf normalizes to -1/0/1 (Collation.Compare clamps, Int32/Int64/Double/Decimal/ObjectId/Guid/BsonArray/byte[] all clamp).
- Comparer consistency: the fast path uses `==` (Collation.Binary via BsonValue.Equals) while the min-scan uses the pragma collation. Binary-equal implies collation-equal, so the asymmetry can only lose an optimization, never reorder — discarded. Verified collation-equal-but-binary-distinct keys (IgnoreCase "A"/"a") still come out contiguous across container boundaries, so GroupByPipe.YieldDocuments' collation-based key equality cannot split a group.
- Container chunk boundaries: YieldValues size accounting matches SortContainer.Insert's offset arithmetic (both `GetKeyLength(key,false) + PageAddress.SIZE`), the overflow item is re-yielded into the next container without double-counting, and no empty container can be produced (so Sort()'s do/while never yields a default KeyValuePair).
- Disposal/abandon: SortService.Dispose is Interlocked-guarded, returns each container position exactly once, disposes containers before returning the shared reader stream, and is reached via the iterator `using` in BasePipe.OrderBy on early abandon. Exceptions thrown from SortService.Insert leave no unreturned disk position.
- DocumentCacheEnumerable / GroupByPipe lifetime: SelectGroupBy disposes each group cache in a `finally` (including on the HAVING `continue`), the drain-on-dispose advances the shared enumerator so GroupBy() cannot spin forever on the same group, and QueryPipe.SelectAll's `drainOnDispose:false` is correct for an aggregate that owns the source.
- Snapshot lifetime under lazy enumeration: TransactionService.Safepoint only calls Snapshot.Clear() (never Dispose), the collection page is deliberately retained, IndexNode.Key is read eagerly in the constructor, and BasePipe.Include's cached CollectionIndex holds only addresses — so Include's cross-safepoint caching is safe.
- Skip/Limit/Offset arithmetic in QueryPipe/GroupByPipe/OrderGroupedResult, and the double-include in SelectAll (a no-op because DoInclude removes `$ref` on the first pass).

Candidates investigated and DISCARDED with reasons:
- Insert.cs relying on the "_id" index being enumerated first when chaining IndexNode.NextNode: safe. CollectionPage._indexes is a Dictionary whose entry 0 is always "_id" (DropIndex("_id") is rejected at Index.cs:174), so "_id" is always enumerated first and always re-serialized first.
- Stale CollectionPage / IndexNode references across transaction.Safepoint() in Insert/Upsert/Update/EnsureIndex: this fork handles it - Snapshot.Clear() retains _collectionPage and refreshes its ownership epoch (SnapShot.cs:132-152), IndexService.FindAll pre-reads the next address before yielding (IndexService.cs:360-363), IndexNode caches NextNode/DataBlock in managed fields, and IndexService.AddNode reloads its `last` parameter to survive page defrag.
- Update.cs comparing old/new index keys with ordinal BsonValue equality while the skip list compares under the collation: produces extra delete+insert work but the resulting index state is correct, and DeleteList always runs before AddNode so a unique index cannot transiently collide with itself.
- Vector index nodes polluting the per-document IndexNode linked list (which would make Update's toDelete destroy them): they do not - vector nodes live in VectorIndexPage/VectorIndexNode and are never chained via NextNode.
- Partial persistence of a multi-document Insert: safepoint-flushed pages are written unconfirmed, and AutoTransaction's rollback (plus ReturnNewPages) leaves them unreferenced, so the insert really is all-or-nothing.
- Orphaned pages after DropCollection: Snapshot.DropCollection is complete - DataPage.FreeIndexSlot always returns a slot in 0..4 so every data page is reachable from FreeDataPageList, and every live index page is reachable via FindAll plus index.Head.
- GetCollectionIndexesSlots() returning null holes after a DropIndex, then NRE in DeleteList/DeleteAll: IndexService.DropIndex removes every node of that slot from every document chain, so no orphan-slot node survives.
- DeleteMany's "_id = value" fast path losing parameters: BsonExpression.SetParameters propagates the parameters document to Left/Right recursively, so predicate.Right.Execute sees them.
- EngineSettings.TransactionPageLimit accepting non-positive values: TransactionMonitor's constructor rejects <= 0, so a bad value fails Open() rather than corrupting safepoint behaviour.

DEFECTS PROVEN BUT OUT OF MY REPORTING SCOPE (they live in LiteDB/Utils/Tokenizer.cs and LiteDB/Engine/SystemCollections/, not in the assigned paths) -- the JSON reader's unescaping actually lives in the Tokenizer, so the "escaping/unescaping on read" lens mostly landed there:
1. Tokenizer.cs:688-698 ParseSingleChar silently returns 0 for a non-hex digit, so ReadString accepts invalid \u escapes and produces a wrong character instead of an error: "\uZZZZ" becomes U+0000. Worse, a truncated escape consumes the closing quote as one of its four hex digits: for {"a":"\u00", "b":1} the string value becomes "\0 " and the separating comma is swallowed, silently re-framing the rest of the document instead of failing (medium; in Tokenizer.cs).
2. Tokenizer.cs:637-650 silently drops unknown escape sequences ("\x41" yields "AB"), and line 648 appends any \u code point including a lone surrogate. A lone surrogate read from JSON is later UTF-8 encoded by BufferWriter, becoming U+FFFD on disk -- an unpaired-surrogate round trip is lossy with no error (low/medium; Tokenizer.cs). JsonWriter's own surrogate handling is correct: each half falls into the default branch and is written as \udXXX, which re-reads as the same pair.
3. SysFileJson.cs:58 opens the output file with FileMode.OpenOrCreate when overwritten:true, which does not truncate. Exporting a smaller result over a larger existing file leaves the previous file's tail bytes after the closing ']', producing a JSON file that fails to re-import (should be FileMode.Create).

EXAMINED AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPORTED: NaN/Infinity written as null (JsonWriter.cs:76-79) and BsonType.Vector written as a plain array (JsonWriter.cs:120-124) are both pinned by existing tests (LiteDB.Tests/Document/Json_Tests.cs:80-109) as intentional, and the vector index coerces arrays back to float[] (VectorIndexService.cs:899-915), so the vector type loss is not a functional break. Decimal, Int64, ObjectId, Guid and Binary round trips are exact. Both ReadObject and ReadArray terminate on EOF (Expect throws), so no infinite-loop path exists on truncated input. JsonWriter.WriteValue is also unboundedly recursive, so a self-referential BsonDocument (d["self"] = d, which nothing prevents) overflows the stack on ToString(); I left that out because BsonValue has no cycle detection anywhere, making it a whole-type issue rather than a JSON one.

- `CollectionPage.InsertCollectionIndex`'s `(byte)(Max(Slot)+1)` slot wrap to 0: requires ~255 live indexes plus a specific create/drop sequence within the 8096-byte index area — too contrived to assert.
- `DiskService.MAX_ITEMS_COUNT` uint multiply overflow: only at ~138 GB of data+log, treated as not realistically reachable.
- HNSW vector-index graph invariants (EnsureBidirectional writing neighbor levels above a node's LevelCount while RemoveNode only cleans `level < LevelCount`, leaving possible dangling neighbor addresses): genuinely suspicious, but proving it needs the full level-assignment invariant across Insert/SearchLayer/GreedySearch, which I could not close within this lens. Flagging it here as the highest-value follow-up.

Candidates investigated and DISCARDED with reasons: (1) path traversal in RunDirectoryPlanner.Sanitize / ReproExecutor.Sanitize - `..` survives sanitisation and PurgeDirectory does a recursive Directory.Delete, but manifest `id` is regex-validated `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` by ManifestValidator and RunCommand always passes manifest.Id (never RawId), while sharedDatabaseKey can only escape one level because '/' and '\\' are in Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() on both platforms - not reachable. (5) `pull_request_target` - not used anywhere; the only `github.event.*` use is correctly passed via env. (6) Unsalted SHA-1 password verifier in FileReaderV7 - fixed legacy v7 on-disk format, read-only upgrade path, cannot be changed without breaking compatibility; reported as out of scope rather than a new defect.
